extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style article summarizing the conception, planned format, objections, and cancellation reasons for a proposed BBC television special on climate change ('Planet Relief').

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial impartiality / avoid proselytising
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC's stance that 'It is not the BBC's job to lead opinion or proselytise on this or any other subject.' (quote from Peter Horrocks). The BBC also rejected framing the programme as saving the planet: 'It is absolutely not the BBC's job to save the planet.' (quote from Peter Barron).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a reason for cancelling Planet Relief — the BBC is wary of programmes that could be seen as campaigning or promoting a particular policy position. The article notes claims that the show 'would be "biased" towards promoting responses based on acceptance of mainstream climate change science,' which raised impartiality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer documentary/factual formats to campaign-style specials
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC stated that 'after Live Earth what audiences say is they are looking for programmes of a documentary or factual nature to explain the complex subject.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides format selection for covering complex issues like climate change: choose documentary/factual approaches rather than overt campaign-style specials if aiming to meet audience expectations and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational safety and feasibility of publicity stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised that the proposed electric power station shutdown 'might overload parts of the [electricity distribution] network.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical/logistical risk assessment is required for plans that involve manipulating infrastructure (e.g., power station shutdowns or public actions urging mass switching off of electricity). The article notes the BBC had spent over a year negotiating the shutdown, highlighting the need for long negotiations with technical operators and consideration of network impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify programme purpose: awareness vs charity
rubrics_metrics.description: Planet Relief 'was not planned to be a charity event, but to increase awareness, similar to Live Earth.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define whether a special is intended as a fundraiser, awareness campaign, documentary, or entertainment event, since purpose influences format, partnerships, and how impartiality concerns are perceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and manage stakeholder and political criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme attracted objections from 'right wing commentators' and 'climate deniers' (e.g., Martin Durkin), while climate activists (e.g., Mark Lynas, Tony Juniper) criticized the cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning high-profile issue-driven programmes, anticipate criticism from multiple political/interest groups and be prepared with engagement, explanation of editorial choices, and mitigation strategies—both to avoid perceptions of bias and to manage reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow sufficient development and negotiation time for complex specials
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme 'had been in development for 18 months' and the BBC 'had spent over a year negotiating' aspects such as the power station shutdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex television specials, especially those involving external partners or infrastructure actions, require lengthy development and negotiation; schedule and resource planning should account for extended lead times and stakeholder approvals.
